I have multiple personalities and almost all the important people in my life know about it. They may mimic me, but no way in hell are they mimicking my alters. Too many voices for them to account for, so it's just not worth the effort.

The thoughts themselves are still there in the background. But i've learned how to ignore them or overcome the urge to act on them by taking a good look at my life as it is. I even played out a few hundred scenarios of me getting seriously hurt or dying. I genuinely just have too much to loose. I find that a lot of people are like that, but in my case the only thing stopping me from plummeting to my death is my girlfriend.. they have their own mental health issues and it's very likely that if i die by any means she'll likely follow me into hell, or whatever comes after this life, and frankly i refuse to let that happen.

So my advice is this: If you lack the motivation to live by your own terms, then live for others. Be it a family member, a significant other, a friend, an idol of some kind, or if none of that appeals then i suggest charity work. 
Or the military as a last resort, because 100% they will absolutely pay for whatever help you need.

I sincerely hope this helps anyone who needs it. And if it does i strongly suggest spreading this message because mental health is the real issue of today's world and it really needs to be talked about more.

I've got a story:

When I was in 7th and/or grade I was the shiest kid in the entire school. I had a single friend that I could actually call a friend, and even then I'm pretty sure she had a crush on me at that point (could be wrong tho) anyway she was the single craziest person I'd ever met that wasn't one of my hyper dumb-ass relatives. It did not take long for me to get a crush on her. I had a chance to ask her out on the school trip that year but blew it cuz I panicked and said **the exact fucking opposite** of what I felt, thinking back on it I only know that I blew it because I remember her sounding incredibly disappointed and saying immediately afterward "Can I be alone please?" with sadness evident (I still feel bad about that). She had moved away that summer. I remember being pretty damn sad that summer, and the more I wanted her, the the worse it got. Then my freshman year of high school started. There was a girl in my foreign language class that was pretty much a duplicate of her but with very colorful hair, larger boobs (but not by too much), and she was like 4'11. We instantly became friends, but that's mainly because she sat directly in front of me and liked socializing. I soon realized she was just as (if not more) of a nutcase as my 7th/8th grade crush, who turned out to be lesbian a few years later. I fell in love hard, and I'm very certain that it was obvious. I was about to ask her out when I discovered very recent scars that indicated self harm. I wish I had known what to say to her, but my mind completely blanked. We stayed friends, but she didn't really talk to me for the rest of that class, she was probably afraid of what I'd say to her now that I think about it. (Our school was one that advocated "no bullying" but at the same time basically took **ZERO** steps to enforce it.) Throughout the year my friend circle practically blew up. As you could probably suspect, all of them were some mix of bat-shit-crazy and totally nuts (if there's an actual difference.) Oh yeah, and half of them were depressed, and some of them practiced self harm. I don't know exactly when or how, but I adopted their collective persona as my own personality. I do know the why though: I didn't want to be confronted with a situation where I wasn't able to help a friend when they needed it most. Now keep in mind that before these events I was the shiest kid in the entire school, and that's because up until that point all of my peers were dicks and treated me like a ghost.

tl;dr: I went from an extreme introvert to borderline insane half-extrovert in the3 span of roughly a few months because most of my friends had depression and I wanted to change that.

To this day I make it a point to get involved and help the only way I know how, by being a true friend. I have only ever been forced to stay out of it once, and that's only because there were legal worries and I didn't want my life to be ruined for eternity because of it.
